Although Friday’s booster recovery failed, the company had already made three previous booster catches, validating the technique. NASA welcomed Saturday’s news. The space agency is paying billions of dollars for Starship to land Artemis astronauts on the moon later this decade and help build a permanent lunar base. Separating neatly from its booster before things went awry, the upper-stage spacecraft soared into orbit and released 26 advanced Starlink satellites. Starship continued circling the world 165 miles (265 kilometres) up, with live views of itself and Earth streaming down via Starlink. Director General of Police C.V. Anand on Saturday inaugurated the SPS OODA Shoot House at the Telangana Greyhounds facility in Rajendranagar, with the unit asked to maintain its strength at no less than 700 personnel, and continue rigorous operational training. The new facility has been named after martyrs Sandeep, Pavan and Sridhar. The DGP called for continuous training in jungle warfare and operations in rugged, hilly terrain, and asked personnel to remain prepared to respond to emergencies, including hijackings and terrorist attacks. 19c537da3dcfd703.title: Total Chess: Martirosyan inflicts first loss on Carlsen
19c537da3dcfd703.summary: Published - November 14, 2026 11:20 pm IST - BUDAPEST Martirosyan posted a win over World No. 1 Magnus Carlsen before drawing the return game. | Photo Credit: Flickr.com Magnus Carlsen suffered his first loss in the Total Chess World Championship Tour pilot as Haik Martirosyan beat the World No. 1 and took the outright Group C lead on the third day of the Fast Classic stage here on Friday. The Armenian won with white before drawing their return encounter, leaving Carlsen winless after six games. Martirosyan had 10 points to Carlsen’s five. R. Vaishali secured her first Fast Classic victory, recovering from a defeat against Bibisara Assaubayeva to win their second meeting with an attack. The split results left the Indian on four points and the Kazakh on eight in Group D. Arjun Erigaisi overturned a difficult position to beat Wesley So with black before drawing the return match. His nine points put him level with Hans Niemann, three behind leader Maxime Vachier-Lagrave. R. Praggnanandhaa drew both games against Vladislav Artemiev in Group B, their first encounter lasting 89 moves. The Indian had four points and Artemiev five. Martirosyan’s attacking victory over Carlsen helped him move one point clear of Anish Giri, who followed a draw against Ian Nepomniachtchi with a win after a long battle. Nepomniachtchi and Shakhriyar Mamedyarov had seven points each. Mamedyarov drew twice against Abhimanyu Mishra, who had five. Vachier-Lagrave drew his game against Niemann before winning the return with white to reach 12 points. So had four. Group B leader Fabiano Caruana beat Vincent Keymer with black and drew their second game. Unbeaten with four wins and two draws, he had 14 points, four clear of Liem Le, who drew twice against Richard Rapport. Keymer had four points and Rapport five. In Group A, Andrew Hong handed Alireza Firouzja his first group-stage defeat before the leader won their return meeting. Firouzja retained top spot with 11 points. Hong had six. Jan-Krzysztof Du

7df78a651aea740f.title: Synod of Jacobite Church approves steps to canonise Patriarch Ignatius Peter III
7df78a651aea740f.summary: Published - November 15, 2026 01:00 am IST - KOCHI The Episcopal Synod of the Jacobite Syrian Church on Saturday (November 14) decided to complete the procedures to canonise Patriarch Ignatius Peter III, who convened the historic Mulanthuruthy Synod in 1876. The decision was taken as Patriarch Ignatius Aphrem II, the supreme head of the Universal Syrian Orthodox Church, accepted the Jacobite Church’s request to declare Ignatius Peter III a saint. A statement by the Jacobite Syrian Church said the decision was taken at a meeting of the Episcopal Synod, chaired by Patriarch Ignatius Aphrem II, at the Marthoman Cathedral in Mulanthuruthy during the 150th anniversary celebrations of the Mulanthuruthy Synod. Addressing the synod, the Patriarch called for collective efforts to establish lasting peace in the Malankara Church. Hailing from Mosul, Ignatius Peter III was the Patriarch of Antioch and head of the Syriac Orthodox Church from 1872 until he died in 1894. 170730d4ae20685c.title: Transport Secretary inspects temporary bus termini in Tiruvannamalai for Karthigai Deepam
170730d4ae20685c.summary: Published - November 15, 2026 05:30 am IST - TIRUVANNAMALAI L. Nirmal Raj, Secretary, Department of Transport, inspect a temporary bus terminus in Tiruvannamalai town in the presence of Collector Vandhana Garg and other officials on Saturday. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement The district administration has set up 26 temporary bus termini on the outskirts of Tiruvannamalai town with over 4,500 special buses, which will be operated between November 22 and 25 for Karthigai Deepam festival. Officials of Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation (TNSTC) said that as part of preparatory works for the festival, L. Nirmal Raj, Secretary, Department of Transport, inspected a few temporary bus termini in the presence of Collector Vandhana Garg, S. Sridharan, Managing Director, TNSTC, and G. Kalaiselvan, deputy general manager (Commercial), TNSTC (Tiruvannamalai). “Basic amenities at the temporary bus termini will be done by the civic body. a29277a425951066.title: Eight varieties of pharmaceutical ingredients worth ₹3.54 lakh seized in TG SAFE raid at Ameenpur firm
a29277a425951066.summary: Published - November 15, 2026 02:00 am IST - HYDERABAD The drugs wing of the Telangana Standards Authority for Food and Essential Drugs (TG SAFE) seized illegally stocked Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs) worth ₹3.54 lakh during a raid at a private company in Sultanpur village of Ameenpur mandal in Sangareddy district. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement The drugs wing of the Telangana Standards Authority for Food and Essential Drugs (TG SAFE) seized illegally stocked Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs) worth ₹3.54 lakh during a raid at a private company in Sultanpur village of Ameenpur mandal in Sangareddy district. The raid was conducted at Neocell Biotechnologies Private Limited, located at the Medical Devices Park in Sultanpur, on Friday, following credible information about the illegal stocking of pharmaceutical ingredients for sale without a valid drug licence. According to TG SAFE, officials found eight varieties of APIs illegally stocked at the premises and seized drug stocks worth ₹3.54 lakh. Further investigation is under way, and action will be initiated against those responsible in accordance with the law, TG SAFE said. They further added that stocking APIs for sale without a valid drug licence is punishable under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, with imprisonment of up to five years. TG SAFE’s Drugs Wing is responsible for issuing licences for the stocking and sale of APIs under the Act. 1a8dffc89945a4da.title: Healthy habits, preventive care key to youth wellbeing, says surgeon
1a8dffc89945a4da.summary: Published - November 15, 2026 01:03 am IST - CHENNAI Cardiac surgeon, healthcare innovator and author Shriram Nene interacts with moderator Vasanthi Hariprakash during a session at the Next Gen Forum. | Photo Credit: Johan Sathya Das J Preventive healthcare and emotional wellbeing must become an integral part of nurturing the next generation, said cardiothoracic surgeon and healthcare innovator Shriram Nene at the NextGen Forum, a two-day conclave on youth safety and wellbeing, which concluded in Chennai on Saturday. Delivering the keynote address titled ‘Before They Become Patients: Why Wellbeing Must Begin Young’, Dr. Nene spoke about the importance of developing healthy habits and prioritising preventive healthcare from an early age. Drawing on his experience in healthcare and his recently released book, ‘21 Days to Good Health’, he highlighted the need to make everyday wellbeing a priority rather than focusing on healthcare only after the onset of illness. He also spoke about the role of emotional wellbeing in ensuring that young people grow up healthy. Organised by The Kindness Foundation on November 13 and 14, the forum brought together over 200 students aged 11 to 17 from more than 20 schools and over 25 experts from 15 sectors. The two-day event featured discussions on youth safety, mental health, digital risks, substance misuse and the challenges faced by young people. The insights from the conclave will contribute to a co-created White Paper on Youth Safety and Wellbeing, which will include young people’s perspectives and recommendations from experts for families, institutions and policymakers, said foundation founder and managing trustee Mahima Poddar. 72599b68cc6a8b03.title: TGPCB recommends closures, forfeitures over dusty construction
72599b68cc6a8b03.summary: Published - November 15, 2026 02:11 am IST The Telangana Pollution Control Board (TGPCB) has received several complaints regarding air pollution caused by dust emissions from construction projects in the Tellapur and Kollur areas of Sangareddy district. After receiving several complaints of air pollution due to construction, the Pollution Control Board (TGPCB) constituted Rolling Task Force Teams to these projects and assess compliance with environmental regulations and implementation of air pollution control measures. The team embarked on inspections and observed dust emissions from construction activity was aggravating air pollution. Several violations of environmental norms were also identified, the TGPCB stated. The Committee reviewed the environmental compliance of as many as 16 construction projects. After examining the severity of the violations, committee recommended the issuing of closure orders against projects where serious violations were identified, along with the forfeiture of bank guarantees. The committee also recommended forfeiture of bank guarantees in respect of projects where minor violations were observed. A period of 10 days was recommended for the concerned projects to rectify the violations. Three construction projects began construction activity without obtaining Consent for Establishment (CFE) from the Pollution Control Board, the TGPCB stated. The committee recommended the issuance of closure orders against these projects, it added. Two others were continuing construction activities in violation of the Orders for Suspension of Operations previously issued by the TGPCB, without obtaining permission from the Board for revocation of the suspension orders. A Ready Mix Concrete plant operating in association with another construction project was found to be functioning without obtaining Consent for Operation (CFO) from the TGPCB. LAKSHMI NARAYANAN The AIADMK has announced a protest on November 18, demanding action over an alleged incident in which M. Ravisankar, the TVK MLA for Thuraiyur and Deputy Speaker of the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly, assaulted a social activist. In a statement, AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami alleged that Karthik Kumar, a social activist who went to meet Mr. Ravisankar to submit grievances, was subjected to a “brutal attack” and “verbal abuse”. c2eea6fd68b63e51.title: Flood-prone areas to be monitored using drones in Chennai
c2eea6fd68b63e51.summary: Published - November 15, 2026 12:35 am IST - Chennai Residents in low-lying and flood-prone neighbourhoods across Chennai could be monitored more closely during the Northeast monsoon, with the Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) planning to deploy drones across all 15 zones for 30 days, to help officials assess conditions on the ground. The initiative is intended to help civic officials keep track of vulnerable locations during periods of heavy rain and improve coordination of response measures. Aerial footage will allow officials to assess the situation in areas that may be difficult to monitor from the ground and identify locations requiring attention. Under the proposed arrangement, one drone and a trained operating team will be stationed in each of the city’s 15 zones, covering the northern, central, and southern regions. The teams will coordinate with zonal officials on the locations to be monitored and the timing of operations, according to officials. Live video feeds will be made available to designated GCC officials, while recorded footage will be handed over for subsequent assessment. The recordings will include details such as the date, time, zone, and location, wherever available. The footage is expected to support officials in assessing ground conditions in vulnerable neighbourhoods and in coordinating their response during the monsoon. The deployment will cover 30 days, with the operating teams required to follow the locations and priorities identified by GCC officials. 10fdc4f1014ce468.title: VIT-A.P. researchers demonstrate low-cost photonic tech for non-invasive disease screening
10fdc4f1014ce468.summary: Published - November 14, 2026 11:45 pm IST - VIJAYAWADA Scientists from CATS Global (CASTLE Advanced Technologies and Systems), Nashik, Maharashtra, and VIT-A.P. University, Amaravati, Andhra Pradesh, have developed and demonstrated an innovative, low-cost optical sensing approach that could pave the way for affordable, non-invasive disease screening through breath analysis. According to a press release from the VIT-A.P., the research article titled ‘Photonic elastic-backscatter fingerprinting of exhaled-breath metabolites for non-invasive disease screening’, authored by professors Rao Tatavarti, Sridevi Nadimpalli and P. Arulmozhivarman Pachiyappan, was published on November 6, 2026, in the international journal Scientific Reports, published by Springer Nature. The study explores a photonic sensing technique that uses a simple, low-power laser and a position-sensitive optical detector to identify distinctive optical signatures associated with disease-related chemical compounds. According to the release, human breath contains hundreds of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) and other gases that can reflect changes in the body’s metabolic processes. Variations in the concentration of these compounds can be associated with different diseases, making breath analysis a promising approach for non-invasive health screening. However, conventional breath-analysis technologies often rely on sophisticated laboratory instruments, including mass spectrometers, gas chromatographs and advanced optical spectroscopy systems, which can be expensive and require specialised infrastructure. The study addresses this challenge, by demonstrating the potential of photonic elastic-backscatter fingerprinting to detect, distinguish and classify different disease-associated gas mixtures through subtle changes in the intensity and spatial position of scattered laser light. This approach offers a direction towards developing compact, cost-effective and potentially portable optical sensing systems,

9fad22104d19b253.title: Past weather trends show fewer cyclones crossing Tamil Nadu coast during Northeast monsoon
9fad22104d19b253.summary: Published - November 15, 2026 01:00 am IST - CHENNAI Senior meteorologists point out that only 22 of the 117 cyclonic systems that formed over the Bay of Bengal during October and November, between 1981 and 2025, made landfall along the State’s coast. | Photo Credit: VELANKANNI RAJ B Tamil Nadu has seen relatively fewer cyclonic systems crossing its coast during the Northeast monsoon in the past 45 years, noted meteorologists. The Bay of Bengal is churning its next cyclone for the season. However, the current predictions indicate the possibility of only less rainfall over the State. Senior meteorologists point out that only 22 of the 117 cyclonic systems that formed over the Bay of Bengal during October and November, between 1981 and 2025, made landfall along the State’s coast. Many of the systems moved northwards towards places such as Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, West Bengal, Bangladesh and the Arakan coast, while others weakened over the sea without crossing any coast. Y.E.A. Raj, former deputy director general of meteorology, Regional Meteorological Centre, Chennai, said 68 of the 117 systems moved north of Tamil Nadu towards the neighbouring States or countries, while 26 dissipated over the Bay of Bengal without making landfall. However, the State has received rainfall during some past years when the system dissipated over the sea. Citing IMD data, he said of the three to four weather systems or cyclones that generally form over the Bay of Bengal between October and December, only one comes closer to or crosses the Tamil Nadu coast. Going by statistics since 1981, Tamil Nadu experiences a coastal crossing roughly once every two years during October and November. The occurrence of three weather systems moving north of Tamil Nadu during October and November is not unprecedented. A similar pattern was recorded in 10 previous years, including 1983, 1996, 2010 and 2013, Mr. Raj added. Published - November 15, 2026 01:00 am IST Terms & conditions | Institutional Subscribe

095d608f305cb939.title: Tamil Nadu unlikely to see significant impact of severe cyclonic storm brewing over Bay of Bengal
095d608f305cb939.summary: Published - November 15, 2026 12:46 am IST - CHENNAI The current weather predictions indicate that the well marked is expected to gain strength as a cyclonic storm and intensify further as a severe cyclonic storm. | Photo Credit: VELANKANNI RAJ B The weather system brewing over the Bay of Bengal is likely to intensify into a severe cyclonic storm by November 18. However, Tamil Nadu may remain largely on the fringes of its impact, according to the Regional Meteorological Centre (RMC). The season’s third cyclone is also likely to bypass Tamil Nadu and impact coastal Andhra Pradesh and Odisha. The current weather predictions indicate that the well marked low-pressure area over southeast Bay of Bengal is expected to gain strength as a cyclonic storm over the central parts of south and adjoining westcentral Bay of Bengal around November 16 evening. It is likely to further intensify into a severe cyclonic storm by November 18. While the weather agency is likely to provide clarity on the system’s movement and likely landfall location only after it consolidates into a depression, heavy rainfall warnings has been largely issued for other States, including Andaman and Nicobar islands, coastal Andhra Pradesh and Odisha, till November 20. The cyclone is likely to be named ‘Akvan’, suggested by Iran under the naming list of tropical cyclones over North Indian Ocean. Officials of the RMC said the possibility of heavy rainfall in Tamil Nadu remained low, given the system’s current position and expected trajectory. Rainfall of light to moderate intensity is likely to be concentrated over the southern and Western Ghats districts till November 20. V.R. Durai, Head, Regional Weather Forecasting Centre, RMC, said there was currently no indication of heavy rainfall over the State. Winds from Arabian sea and a minor system over south Tamil Nadu would trigger rainfall over the southern and Western Ghats districts. Major weather disturbances usually form in the southwest Bay of Bengal duri

22f9a332bcfc3b19.title: Vijayawada Press Club to organise blood donation camp on November 16
22f9a332bcfc3b19.summary: Published - November 14, 2026 11:19 pm IST - VIJAYAWADA The Vijayawada Press Club and the NTR Memorial Trust Blood Centre are jointly organising a free blood donation camp on November 16 to mark National Press Day. The camp will be held at the Press Club in Gandhi Nagar from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. on Monday. CR Media Academy Chairman Alapati Suresh Kumar will be the chief guest and inaugurate the camp. Donors will be issued certificates by the NTR Trust. Those holding the certificates can avail themselves of blood transfusion services from the Trust at half the regular price if they need them in the future, according to a release. Journalists willing to donate blood have been requested to register their names in advance at the Press Club. 42450c98eac177bc.title: SCoR, Central Bank of India ink pact to extend welfare facilities for railway staff
42450c98eac177bc.summary: Published - November 14, 2026 11:49 pm IST - VIJAYAWADA Officials of the South Coast Railway (SCoR), Vijayawada Division, signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Central Bank of India, for extending more welfare facilities to railway employees. Additional Divisional Railway Manager (ADRM-Infrastructure) P. E. Edwin and Central Bank of India, Hyderabad Region, General Manager M. Pichai signed the MoU on Friday, aimed at providing enhanced financial and banking facilities to the employees. As per the MoU, railway employees are eligible for salary accounts with zero balance, personal accident and term insurance coverage up to ₹1.5 crore and other benefits. SCoR Vijayawada Division Senior Personal Officer Prem Kumar Lakhawat, bank Vijayawada regional head E. Venkateswara Rao, Guntur regional head G. V. Ramana Rao and other officials were present. 282873a6223dae89.title: Manipur probe panel gets sixth extension; no sign of report yet
282873a6223dae89.summary: Updated - November 14, 2026 01:12 am IST - NEW DELHI The panel is probing the sequence of events and facts relating to the ethnic violence that broke out in the State on May 3, 2023, after a “Tribal Solidarity March” was organised in the hill districts. File | Photo Credit: ANI The three-member Commission of Inquiry, set up by the Union Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) to probe the 2023 Manipur ethnic violence, was given a sixth extension on Friday. The Ministry notified that the commission, which was constituted on June 4, 2023, “shall submit its report to the Central government as soon as possible but not later than May 20, 2027”. More than 300 people have been killed in the ethnic violence that erupted between the Kuki-Zo and Meitei people on May 3, 2023. Around 60,000 people have been displaced from their homes. The probe panel’s report is awaited even as the ethnic conflict has now spread to the Kuki and Naga communities. Since February this year, more than 60 people have been killed in Naga-Kuki clashes. The commission is now headed by former Supreme Court judge Balbir Singh Chauhan, after Ajai Lamba, the former Chief Justice of the Gauhati High Court, resigned as the chairperson of the panel in February this year. The panel is yet to finalise its report. Justice (retd.) Chauhan is also heading the judicial inquiry into an incident of violence that occurred in Ladakh’s Leh city on September 24, 2025 where four civilians, including a Kargil war veteran, were killed in police firing. The Ladakh report is yet to be submitted to the government. Manipur’s Commission of Inquiry has received around 11,000 affidavits. President’s rule was imposed in the State on February 13, 2025 and on February 4 this year, a new Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh took oath, ending Central rule. In the previous week, the forex reserves had dropped by USD 2.691 billion to USD 717.056 billion. The reserves had touched an all-time high of USD 785.706 billion during the week ended September 4, driven by a heavy flow of currency as part of a special concessional swap for deposits from the diaspora through which banks raised a record USD 133 billion, but had been on a decline ever since. During the week ended November 6, foreign currency assets, a major component of reserves, increased by USD 232 million to USD 591.350 billion, according to the data released by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). 09a099c026b5c94a.title: Rajya Sabha panel visits ISRO, HAL facilities in Bengaluru
09a099c026b5c94a.summary: Published - November 14, 2026 12:41 am IST - Bengaluru The committee also visited the Indian Space Research Organisation’s U.R. Rao Satellite Centre which is the county’s lead centre for building satellites and developing associated satellite technologies. | Photo Credit: K. Murali Kumar Members of the Subordinate Legislation Committee of Rajya Sabha on Friday visited key defence, space and finance institutions in Bengaluru as part of a study visit. The committee, led by Chairman Milind Deora, visited the Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL), toured the LCA Tejas Division and witnessed a static display of the defence PSU’s various platforms. The HAL said the committee reviewed the implementation of the Companies (Corporate Social Responsibility) Rules, 2014. “HAL Chairman Ravi K., and Director (HR), M.G. Balasubrahmanya, and other senior officials were present during the interaction, which provided an opportunity to showcase the HAL’s contributions to indigenous aerospace development and its commitment to impactful and sustainable CSR initiatives,” the HAL said. The committee also visited the Indian Space Research Organisation’s U.R. Rao Satellite Centre which is the county’s lead centre for building satellites and developing associated satellite technologies. “The committee got a closer look at India’s satellite capabilities and discussed the future of our space sector from liberalisation and reusable rockets to Chandrayaan missions, space debris and e-waste regulations. While India’s space ambitions are reaching new heights, our sustainability game must keep up. Innovation and responsibility must go hand-in-hand,” Mr. Deora posted on X. The committee also held meetings with officials of the Reserve Bank of India and leading Public Sector Unit (PSU) banks to discuss the future of digital payment security. 2a18505d20b9e62f.title: Former MIDS Director P.G. Babu no more
2a18505d20b9e62f.summary: Published - November 14, 2026 12:31 am IST - Chennai P.G. Babu, former Director, Madras Institute of Development Studies. | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT P.G. Babu, former Director, Madras Institute of Development Studies, passed away in Dindigul, his hometown, on Thursday. He was 65 and is survived by his mother, a brother, and a sister. Prof. Babu was serving as the Vice-Chancellor of Vidyashilp University, Bengaluru, since 2023. During his tenure as the Director of MIDS between 2019 and 2022, he brought out a series of books in both Tamil and English, most notably on the economic policy during the pandemic. For over three decades, he had served at the Indira Gandhi Institute of Development Research, Mumbai, where he was also the Dean of Graduate Studies and coordinated the Law and Economics programmes. His research focussed on Microeconomic theory and Game theory with applications across Environmental and Natural Resource Economics, Law and Economics, and Politics-Philosophy and Economics. His research contributions include work on the decision-making framework for climate change as part of the IPCC working group, which earned him a citation from the Prime Minister of India. Prof. Babu was serving as the Vice-Chancellor of Vidyashilp University, Bengaluru, since 2023. During his tenure as the Director of MIDS between 2019 and 2022, he brought out a series of books in both Tamil and English, most notably on the economic policy during the pandemic. For over three decades, he had served at the Indira Gandhi Institute of Development Research, Mumbai, where he was also the Dean of Graduate Studies and coordinated the Law and Economics programmes. His research focussed on Microeconomic theory and Game theory with applications across Environmental and Natural Resource Economics, Law and Economics, and Politics-Philosophy and Economics. His research contributions include work on the decision-making framework for climate change as part of the IPCC working group, which earned him a citation from the Prime Minister of India. 0833c1b532f61694.title: Germany open to discussing critical mineral partnerships with India, says Ambassador
0833c1b532f61694.summary: Updated - November 14, 2026 12:01 am IST - COIMBATORE German Ambassador to India Jasper Wieck (right) visited the Gedee Technical Training Institute in Coimbatore city on Friday. | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRAGEMENT Germany’s Ministry of Economic Affairs has critical mineral partnerships already with a range of countries. With India, the channels are open to discuss how to enhance the cooperation in that domain, German Ambassador to India Jasper Wieck told The Hindu in Coimbatore on Friday. Asked about increasing recycling of industrial waste in European countries and its impact on raw material supplies to Indian companies, he said Germany also supports the Indian government in promoting and making progress in recycling and recovering industrial waste. One aspect, for example, is recycling of old solar panels because the raw materials are needed and China is increasing its export curbs. Germany is ready to further engage with India on critical minerals in order to work on sustainable solutions and securing supply chains. India and Germany share the destiny of being short of critical minerals. Circular economy is a strong part of the India-Germany Green and Sustainable Development Partnership. It will be further enhanced. But, the thrust is to support India in increasing its own recycling quota, the Ambassador said. Mr. Wieck, who visited the Gedee Technical Training Institute (GTTI) in Coimbatore, said, “Germany is keen on sharing its experience in vocational training with India. In the framework of our development cooperation, we have many programmes that encourage Indian companies to provide for training on the spot in close cooperation, for instance, with Indian technical institutes,” he said. Germany already recognises Indian dual vocational training certificates thereby enabling a smooth transition into the German labour market, if needed. f647fe46dbf1ca20.title: ABB India Q3CY26 results: Net profit rises 11% to ₹440 cr, revenue up 19.4%
f647fe46dbf1ca20.summary: Electrification and automation major ABB India on Friday posted an 11 per cent rise in net profit to Rs 440 crore in the September quarter compared to the year-ago period, driven by higher revenues. The company follows a January-December fiscal year. The net profit was Rs 398 crore in the quarter ended on September 30, 2025, an exchange filing showed. Revenues from operations rose to Rs 3,738 crore in the quarter from Rs 3,130 crore in the same period a year ago. ABB India Managing Director Sanjeev Sharma said, "We delivered a strong third quarter, with record Q3 orders, revenue growth and a healthy backlog reflecting continued customer confidence in ABB's technology and solutions." He stated that the demand remained broad-based across industries, supported by investments in productivity, energy efficiency and sustainable growth. Looking ahead, he stated that India's structural growth drivers in industrialisation, electrification, digitalisation and the energy transition continue

f3a26d1288f5f710.title: Vigilance Awareness Week concludes at NLCIL
f3a26d1288f5f710.summary: Published - November 14, 2026 05:30 am IST - CUDDALORE Prasanna Kumar Acharya, Chairman and Managing Director of NLCIL, presenting the Most Vigilant Employee Award to an employee at the valedictory function in Cuddalore on Thursday. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement Prasanna Kumar Acharya, chairman and managing director of NLC India Limited (NLCIL) has called for greater transparency and visibility in organisational systems in NLCIL, and the elimination of manual interventions. He was speaking at the valedictory function of the Vigilance Awareness Week 2026 in Neyveli on Thursday. Speaking at the meeting, Mr. Acharya said that contract manuals and operational procedures were being updated to strengthen accountability and ensure seamless governance. He appreciated the Vigilance Division’s outreach and preventive initiatives organised under the Central Vigilance Commission’s (CVC) theme, ‘Probity for Prosperity’. Chief Vigilance Officer (CVO) Appakannu Govindarajan said that this year’s CVC guidelines reflected a shift from focusing on corruption to proactively promoting integrity, honesty, and probity. With NLCIL preparing for large-scale expansion, reducing procedural errors, strengthening capacity building, and keeping pace with technological advances were essential for innovation and sustained growth, a press release quoted him as having said. Highlighting public participation in the campaign, Mr. Govindarajan said reels and rangoli competitions had attracted people from different sections of society. He also stressed the contribution of employees and students to societal development. Director (Mines) Suresh Chandra Suman recalled Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel’s contribution to nation-building and commended the Vigilance Division for involving the public in the campaign. A special edition of NLCIL’s in-house vigilance magazine, Neyveli Vigil, was released on the occasion. Mr. Acharya, functional directors Samir Swarup, Rajesh Pratap Singh Sisodia, P.L.S.S. Chaitanya

4261476b303c73f9.title: Comply with new prices of 137 anti-cancer drugs or face action, says regulator
4261476b303c73f9.summary: Published - November 14, 2026 01:24 am IST - NEW DELHI The revised prices for the 137 anti-cancer drugs came into effect on November 9, 2026, following a gazette order issued on October 17, 2026. The order capped the trade margin on these medicines at 30%. File image used for representation | Photo Credit: Getty Images/iStockphoto The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) has warned of penal action against those failing to comply with the revised prices of 137 non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs The authority, which functions under the Department of Pharmaceuticals, has asked State drug controllers (SDCs) to strictly monitor the prices and submit their action taken reports by November 16, according to an official release on Friday (November 13, 2026). The revised prices for the 137 anti-cancer drugs came into effect on November 9, 2026, following a gazette order issued on October 17, 2026. The order capped the trade margin on these medicines at 30%. Based on submissions received from pharmaceutical companies up to November 11, the latest revised price lists have been uploaded on the NPPA website as well as the Pharma Sahi Daam app and portal, the Chemicals and Fertilizers Ministry said. All manufacturers, stockists, dealers, retailers, hospitals, and medical institutions have been directed to comply with the revised prices and prominently display the updated price lists at their premises and on their websites. The SDCs have been instructed to strictly monitor compliance across the supply chain and healthcare facilities to ensure that the benefits of the revised maximum retail prices (MRPs) are passed on to patients. Any violation of the directive may attract overcharging proceedings under the provisions of the DPCO, 2013, the release noted. Complaints regarding overcharging, shortage, or non-availability of medicines can be reported through the Pharma Sahi Daam app or portal, the NPPA helpline (1800-111-255), or via email at monitoring-nppa@gov.in, it added.

a85d2bf44a8cf4e9.title: Edelweiss Financial Services Q2 FY27 results: Profit rises 18% to ₹207 cr
a85d2bf44a8cf4e9.summary: Edelweiss Financial Services on Friday reported an 18 per cent growth in consolidated net profit to Rs 207 crore for the second quarter ended September. The company had earned a profit of Rs 175 crore in the corresponding quarter of the preceding fiscal. Total income increased to Rs 2,602 crore in the second quarter of FY27, compared to Rs 1,900 crore in the year-ago period, Edelweiss Financial Services said in a regulatory filing. Interest income rose to Rs 720 crore from Rs 687 crore in the same quarter a year ago. During the quarter, total expenses also rose to Rs 2,393 crore from Rs 1,946 crore in the same period a year ago. The company completed the Rs 1,200-crore IPO of its subsidiary Edelweiss Alternatives last month. Earlier this year, global investment management firm Carlyle became a strategic majority investor in another subsidiary of the company, Nido Home Finance, with an investment of Rs 2,000 crore.

054e4d7fccd674ae.title: BIM, Texas university to offer course on AI in Business from next year
054e4d7fccd674ae.summary: Published - November 14, 2026 12:44 am IST - Chennai Bharathidasan Institute of Management (BIM), in collaboration with the University of Texas at Arlington (UTA) in the U.S., on Friday announced the launch of the Master of Science programme in Artificial Intelligence for Business (MSAIB), which is aimed at working professionals in India. On Friday, representatives of the two institutions exchanged Memoranda of Understanding for the course. The first batch of the course will start in August 2027. The first cohort will include 25 students, mostly working professionals, who are keen to upgrade their skills to secure better job opportunities in multinational companies, and the tuition fee is indicated to be around $27,000. Asit K. Barma, Director, BIM, told presspersons in Chennai that the classes would be held at the IIT-Madras Research Park. The location, being a technology hub, will be beneficial to students in terms of access to industry interactions. The conventional MBA course had, over the past few years, been losing its shine gradually, indicated by the falling enrolment for the Common Admission Test (CAT). Last year, there was a 2% drop in students taking the Common Admission Test compared to the previous year, Dr. Barma said. The two-year MSAIB course will provide an opening for young professionals to pursue an industry-oriented course, he said. Fernando Jaramillo, Associate Dean, College of Business, UTA, said the course would be offered in hybrid mode, with faculty members from the UTA visiting the Chennai campus for conducting classes. The curriculum for the course would be the same as the one offered at its Arlington campus. Radha K. Mahapatra, Chair and Professor, Information Systems and Operations Management, UTA, said the faculty for each course would spend about a week on the Chennai campus, while the rest of the classes would be conducted online. 7ef746d78b58d251.title: India imports over half its edible oil, faces food risks: NITI Aayog VC
7ef746d78b58d251.summary: India is perhaps still not secure regarding its food supply across the various products, as the country is the world's largest importer of edible oils, NITI Aayog vice-chairman Ashok Kumar Lahiri said on Friday. Addressing an event here, Lahiri said India meets more than half of its edible oil needs through imports, and imports are estimated at 17 million metric tonnes, valued at about USD 20 billion. Similarly, India is both the world's largest producer and consumer of pulses, and accounts for roughly a fourth of total global pulse consumption, approximately 25 to 27 million tonnes annually. "We are talking about Viksit Krishi in Viksit Bharat in 2047. As we move towards Viksit Bharat at 2047, are we secure regarding our food supply across the various products? Perhaps not as yet," he said. Lahiri observed that he was surprised to learn that chana (gram) which Indians eat comes from Australia, lentils masoor dal from Australia and Canada, and some pulses come from Myanmar, Africa,

2a3d723d92011081.title: Tamil Nadu engages realty developers to fast track Global Capability Centre corridors
2a3d723d92011081.summary: Published - November 14, 2026 12:59 am IST - CHENNAI To advance the implementation of the Tamil Nadu GCC Corridor and Development Programme, the Department of Industries, Investment Promotion and Commerce, Government of Tamil Nadu, convened a roundtable discussion at Guidance Tamil Nadu on Friday with leading real estate developers from Tamil Nadu and across the country, in the presence of Industries Minister S. Keerthana. According to details shared by Guidance, the discussion focused on accelerating the development of Grade-A office space and supporting infrastructure across the identified corridors to meet the needs of the state’s growing Global Capability Centre (GCC) ecosystem. The roundtable brought together developers’ perspectives on strengthening these corridors as integrated destinations for GCC investment and growth. Tamil Nadu is home to more than 460 GCCs, including over 405 in Chennai, with the sector adding more than 55,000 jobs in 2025. Continued expansion by existing centres, alongside interest from new investors, has increased the need for readily available, high-quality office space. Participants discussed measures to accelerate project development, maintain competitive rentals and ensure that suitable space is available within the timelines required by global companies. Developers shared their perspectives on land availability, development costs, floor space index (FSI), approval processes and infrastructure requirements. The discussion emphasised the importance of developing complete GCC ecosystems in Rajiv Gandhi Salai (OMR), Pallavaram–Thoraipakkam Radial Road (PTR) and Mount–Poonamallee High Road (MPR) through mixed-use projects that integrate offices with housing, schools, healthcare, hospitality and retail. Public transport, last-mile connectivity and pedestrian access were identified as essential to supporting the growth of these corridors. Participants noted and appreciated the greater transparency and accountability they had experienced

5c01144be5e1a2d0.title: Modi comes to aid of elderly woman who felt unwell at Mysuru event
5c01144be5e1a2d0.summary: Published - November 14, 2026 12:02 am IST - MYSURU Prime Minister Narendra Modi personally came to the aid of an elderly woman who felt unwell during the inauguration of the COSMOS Planetarium in Mysuru on Friday. The woman, Prema Simbaiah, former president of Nanjangud Town Municipality and a BJP worker, appeared to feel dizzy and was on the verge of collapsing. Noticing her condition, Mr. Modi went up to her and ensured that she received immediate attention. She was given juice to help her recover. Union Minister for Finance and Corporate Affairs Nirmala Sitharaman was also present at the event. Mysuru district BJP president Subbanna later visited Ms. Simbaiah at her residence to enquire about her health. He said she was doing well. Thanking Mr. Modi for coming to her aid, Ms. Simbaiah said she had felt uncomfortable as she had not had lunch before arriving at the venue. She expressed her gratitude to the Prime Minister for providing her with juice and ensuring that she recovered. 9bad3be65f765bb1.title: Over 7,000 books removed from District Central Libraries in Vellore, nearby districts
9bad3be65f765bb1.summary: Published - November 14, 2026 12:39 am IST - VELLORE The library in Ranipet. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement As many as 7,995 books published by the controversial Agalvilakku and Phoenix Publications were removed from the racks of District Central Library in Vellore, Ranipet, Tirupattur, and Tiruvannamalai districts on Friday. The action comes against the backdrop of allegations of fake and AI-generated books being procured from these publishers for public libraries including Periyar Arivulagam, a newly inaugurated public library in Coimbatore. “The identified books of the two publications were removed from the other books. The books, which are meant for distribution to branch libraries in the district for 2025-26, are stored in a separate room,” S. Valli, District Library Officer (Tiruvannamalai), told The Hindu. Ranipet and Tirupattur have the highest number (2,401) of books each from these publications, followed by Tiruvannamalai (2,209 books), and Vellore (984 books). “Books on competitive examinations are a big attraction in District Central library as the facility has a large collection of books related to general knowledge,” said G. Satish, a reader. Officials said District Central Library in these districts have books on subjects including history, politics, law, economics, philosophy, agriculture, computer and mathematics. Reference books, especially for examinations conducted by the Tamil Nadu Public Service Commission (TNPSC), UPSC, and other competitive exams are available. As per norms, around 60,000 to 70,000 books are procured for each district library annually based on feedback provided by local librarians and readers. These books then distributed branch libraries in the district. As per estimates, Vellore and Tiruvannamalai have at least 120 branch libraries each whereas Ranipet and Tirupattur have around 50 branch libraries each. Published - November 14, 2026 12:39 am IST Terms & conditions | Institutional Subscriber Comments have to be in Engl

599ef64f8dbe8628.title: Two men die as van rams tree in Tirupattur
599ef64f8dbe8628.summary: Updated - November 14, 2026 12:41 am IST - TIRUPATTUR Two men and two cows killed after a van hit a roadside tree at Pudur village near Vaniyambadi town in Tirupattur on Friday. Police said K. Bhoopathy, 62, and V. Sankar, 28, both dairy farmers near Alangayam town, were taking the cows on the van to sell them at the weekly cattle market in Uthangarai village near Hosur. Bhoopathy’s son Manikandan, 28, and two other farmers Murugesan, 58, and Krishnan, 56, were also travelling with them. Police said that Manikandan lost control of the vehicle and rammed a roadside tree. In the impact, Manikandan and Sankar, sustained severe injuries and succumbed on the way to hospital. The two cows were killed. The other three men are under treatment. The incident occurred around 4 a.m. The Kavalur police have registered a case. Its revenue from operations declined to Rs 967.3 crore in the second quarter of FY27 from Rs 1,363 crore a year ago, the company said in a regulatory filing. f0d9913262eff5d1.title: Delhi HC takes suo motu cognisance of illegal construction on Sriniwaspuri drain
f0d9913262eff5d1.summary: Published - November 14, 2026 06:22 am IST High Court of Delhi entrance gate. The Delhi High Court has taken suo motu cognisance of the condition of the Sriniwaspuri drain, citing its significant impact on waterlogging in the area and rampant illegal constructions on and around it. A Bench of Justice Prathiba M. Singh and Justice Manmeet P.S. Arora, while disposing of an appeal filed by residents of Sriniwaspuri, directed that the matter be converted into a fresh suo motu petition. The development came after the appellants, who had approached the court seeking proper maintenance, cleaning and reconstruction of drains in the area, sought permission to withdraw their appeal, stating that they did not wish to pursue the proceedings because of the continuous threats they were facing from local residents. In its November 5 order, the court allowed the appellants to withdraw their petition but made it clear that the larger public interest issues concerning the drain could not be ignored. “Owing to the large-scale impact of the drain on the general waterlogging in the area, as also the rampant illegal construction upon and around the drain, this is a fit case for the Court to not ignore the facts that have come to light in the various reports, including the recent inspection report of the Integrated Drain Management Cell (IDMC),” the court said. “Accordingly, the Court takes suo motu cognisance of the situation relating to the Sriniwaspuri drain. Let the inspection report filed by the IDMC and the status report filed by the DJB and other authorities in this case be moved to the new file of the writ petition titled ‘Re: Suo Motu Sriniwaspuri Drain’,” the court ordered. 97fc796799d8e5cb.title: Four-day Chhath festival begins in Bihar with Nahay Khay
97fc796799d8e5cb.summary: Published - November 14, 2026 01:10 am IST - PATNA Devotees arrive to offer prayers and take a holy dip in the Ganga River on 'Nahay Khay', the first day of Chhath Puja, in Patna on November 13, 2026. | Photo Credit: ANI Bihar’s famous Chhath festival began on Friday (November 13, 2026) with Nahay Khay on the first of four days of festivities. A large number of devotees gathered at ghats by rivers, including the Ganga, to collect water and bathe. The festival is performed with piety and the strict observance of fasts to express gratitude to the Sun God for sustaining life on Earth. There are no formal rituals or priests present, and devotion is central to the prayers. The people of Purvanchal (eastern Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Jharkhand) celebrate Chhath Puja on a grand scale. On the first day, all Chhath vratis (devotees holding fasts) bathe in the morning and offer prayers to the rising Sun before partaking in rice and pumpkin curry. On the second day, Kharna, roti and kheer are cooked as prasad in the evening, followed by two continuous days of fasting. On the third day, devotees offer arghya (obeisance) to the setting Sun at the ghats of rivers or temporary water bodies created by the State government, continuing their fast. The Chhath festival this year will conclude on November 16 after devotees offer arghya to the rising Sun on the fourth day, marking the end of the fast. Out of 103 ghats in Patna, 90 have been declared safe for devotees, while 13 have been declared unsafe this year. Chhath Puja is also being celebrated in over a dozen parks in Patna, which already have fountains and water bodies, including Eco Park, Harding Park, Naveen Sinha Park, Lal Bahadur Shastri Park, AG Colony Park, Urja Park, CID Colony Park, and Lohia Nagar Park, and the lake at the Patna Zoo. 406209c89fb3f98c.title: Man held for setting house on fire in Vellore
406209c89fb3f98c.summary: Updated - November 14, 2026 01:01 am IST - VELLORE The house that was gutted. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement A 54-year-old man was arrested by the Veppankuppam police on charges of setting on fire his daughter’s house at Agaram village near Odugathur town at foothills of Jawadhu Hills in Vellore on Friday. Police said the accused R. Anandan, 54, a wage labourer, was upset over his daughter Vaishnavi marrying Rajesh, a milk van driver, against his wishes. In a fit of rage, Anandan allegedly set on fire Rajesh’s father Kumar’s house in Agaram village. Residents alerted Veppankuppam police, who rushed to the spot with firefighters. The house, which was unoccupied, was gutted. A case was registered and Anandan was arrested. b5c068430899b0b2.title: Dietary advice from staff nurses help in blood sugar control in Chennai, counselling to be scaled up
b5c068430899b0b2.summary: Published - November 14, 2026 12:36 am IST - CHENNAI A flat lay of colorful whole foods — fruits, vegetables, nuts, legumes, and spices — arranged for an anti-inflammatory diet. The image conveys balance, vitality and a holistic approach to health through the power of natural foods. Copy space for text, directly above - healthy food, autoimmune disease | Photo Credit: Nathalie Pellenkoft A year-long trial by the Indian Council of Medical Research-National Institute of Epidemiology (ICMR-NIE) and the Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) found that simple dietary advice from staff nurses helped improve blood sugar control among persons with diabetes. Based on the findings, the GCC is planning to roll out the nurse-led diabetes diet advice programme across its 140 Urban Primary Health Centres (UPHCs) in the city. The GCC and ICMR-NIE enrolled 333 adults with type 2 diabetes at 16 UPHCs in four zones between November 2024 and February 2025. These 16 centres were randomly divided into two groups. In eight centres, GCC’s own Non-Communicable Disease (NCD) staff nurse gave a few minutes of one-to-one-advice at each three-monthly visit, while the other eight centres provided usual care, Joshua Chadwick, Scientist, ICMR-NIE, Chennai, who led the study, said. “Most of the persons enrolled were women (72%), with an average age of 56. Their diabetes was poorly controlled. The average HbA1c (a measure of blood sugar over the past three months) was 9.8%, against a target of 7%,” he said. What was their advice on? The nurses told the patients to fill only a quarter of the plate with rice, to cut down on biscuits, sweets, and sugary drinks, and to add more vegetables and affordable protein such as dal, groundnuts, egg, fish, buttermilk. They were advised to take medicines regularly, sleep well, manage stress, move more, do flexibility exercises, including yoga, he said. In eight centres, GCC’s own Non-Communicable Disease (NCD) staff nurse gave a few minutes of one-to-one-advice at each three-monthly visit, while the other eight centres provided usual care, Joshua Chadwick, Scientist, ICMR-NIE, Chennai, who led the study, said. “Most of the persons enrolled were women (72%), with an average age of 56. Their diabetes was poorly controlled. The average HbA1c (a measure of blood sugar over the past three months) was 9.8%, against a target of 7%,” he said. What was their advice on? The nurses told the patients to fill only a quarter of the plate with rice, to cut down on biscuits, sweets, and sugary drinks, and to add more vegetables and affordable protein such as dal, groundnuts, egg, fish, buttermilk. They were advised to take medicines regularly, sleep well, manage stress, move more, do flexibility exercises, including yoga, he said. 7f05c1744b84c178.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday said steps taken in the last decade helped the country to sail through the crisis emerged during the war in the Middle East. He was inaugurating various welfare projects worth over Rs 15,600 crore here, including renewable energy and petroleum infrastructure. "War around Iran and Gulf countries shows how important energy security is. Steps taken for energy security in the last decade helped the country face the crisis with resilience," the PM said. Regarding the Metro Pink Line, which was dedicated to the public, Modi said it gives better connectivity to people in Bengaluru. He also noted that the Metro rail network increased from 17 km in 2014 to over 100 km in 2026 in Bengaluru. On the occasion, Modi lauded Karnataka Governor Sudha Yadav for serving the nation as the widow of a Kargil war hero.

88274b4b7367c7de.title: Bengal draft voter list on Nov 23, final electoral rolls on Jan 16
88274b4b7367c7de.summary: The Election Commission will publish the draft electoral rolls for West Bengal on November 23, with the final voters' list scheduled to be released on January 16, 2027, as part of a Special Summary Revision (SSR), a statement said on Friday. The revision will be conducted with January 1, 2027, as the qualifying date, allowing those who turn 18 by then to enrol as voters, it said. According to the schedule announced by the Chief Electoral Officer's (CEO) office, electors can submit claims and objections between November 23 and December 22. The disposal of applications will be completed by January 8. Special campaign days will be held at designated polling stations across the state on November 28 and 29, and December 5, 6, 12, 13, 19 and 20 to facilitate public participation, the statement said. Booth Level Officers (BLOs) will be available at polling stations on these days to assist voters with fresh enrolment, correction of particulars and submission of claims and objections. Boot

cd2365c62a5f3777.summary: Updated - November 14, 2026 01:08 am IST India’s much-hyped domestic economic resilience is set to be tested over the next few months as external factors start to impose inescapable pressures. A case in point is inflation. The latest data on retail inflation show that it crossed the Reserve Bank of India’s 6% upper comfort limit in October 2026. According to economists, this is likely to continue through the third quarter of this financial year, which means at least two more months of high inflation. Agricultural shortfalls brought on by a patchy and deficient monsoon have meant that food inflation rose sharply to 8.5% in October 2026. Elevated fuel prices meant that inflation in the transport category also rose sharply. What is worse is that high inflation is spreading to almost every aspect of a household’s day-to-day needs. In fact, the latest Consumer Price Index (CPI) data show that 10 of the 12 major categories saw inflation in October, hitting their highest levels recorded in the new series of the index. So, things such as clothing, footwear, housing, furnishings, and services such as healthcare, education, communication, recreation, and restaurant and hospitality are not only getting more expensive, but they are doing so at an accelerating rate. This would have been bad enough had wages been increasing in real terms. Yet, the latest research by Data for India on the country’s official wage statistics shows that, while nominal wages doubled from 2012 to 2024, they actually fell 4% over the same period after adjusting for inflation. And this is sharper for high-skilled and high-earning workers. Lower wage earners saw marginal increases over this period. While this is of some comfort, it is the higher wage earners that drive consumption in an economy. Real wage contraction for them, which is likely to have worsened in 2026, will hit consumption levels and private investment. 6be81aa7223ce5c1.summary: Essar Group's IT firm Black Box on Friday reported a 30.6 per cent increase in consolidated net profit to Rs 72.68 crore for the July-September quarter of FY27, aided by growth in data centre and enterprise businesses. The Mumbai-headquartered company had posted a net profit of Rs 55.65 crore in the year-ago period, according to a regulatory filing by the company. Black Box's revenue from operations rose 22.2 per cent to Rs 1,936.30 crore, up from Rs 1,584.59 crore in Q2 FY26. Sequentially, the profit and revenue rose 30 per cent and 13 per cent, respectively. Growth was driven by execution across hyperscale data centre infrastructure and enterprise solutions, supported by growing momentum in its technology products business, the company said in a statement. Black Box secured over USD 250 million in data centre orders in the first half of FY27. b8602c9e790f5ba7.title: Librarian P.V. Konnur felicitated on his 75th birth anniversary
b8602c9e790f5ba7.summary: Published - November 14, 2026 12:32 am IST - Bengaluru Friends, colleagues and admirers of P.V. Konnur, the library science professional and president of LIS Academy, Bengaluru, felicitated him on his 75th birth anniversary. The Amruta Mahotsava was held at the Dr. Manmohan Singh Bengaluru City University on Thursday. Ramesh B., Vice-Chancellor of Dr. Manmohan Singh Bengaluru City University, released the felicitation volume brought out in Prof. Konnur’s honour and he said that such a dedicated librarian is very hard to find today, and that Prof. Konnur is a role model for budding librarians. He observed that the librarian’s role has become more challenging, as students now have to be drawn back to libraries from their mobile phones. He urged Prof. Konnur to lead this movement and to help university libraries become experiential centres. 603400d77cfff554.title: India’s TB deaths fall 38% since 2015, outpacing global decline: WHO report
603400d77cfff554.summary: New Delhi: India has recorded a 38% reduction in tuberculosis (TB) mortality since 2015, outperforming the global decline of 35%, the Union health ministry said on Thursday. Highlighted in the World Health Organization’s (WHO) Global Tuberculosis Report 2026 released on Thursday, the findings also showed that the country achieved a 94% treatment success rate among drug-susceptible TB patients. According to the WHO report, India’s estimated TB mortality rate dropped from 280 per million people in 2015 to 180 per million in 2025. Meanwhile, a nationally representative TB prevalence survey conducted in 2025 by the Indian Council of Medical Research—National Institute for Research in Tuberculosis (ICMR-NIRT) has been shared with the WHO. The findings are currently under technical review, after which the WHO will publish an updated country profile for India. The health ministry added that 96% of India’s TB programme funding requirements are now met through domestic resources. The ministry also highlighted how the TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan has transformed detection through technological innovation. Between December 2024 and November 2026, more than 250 million people were brought under TB screening. Authorities conducted over 11 crore chest X-rays—using portable, AI-enabled diagnostic tools—alongside more than 30 million rapid molecular nucleic acid amplification tests (NAAT). This identified 4.86 million new TB cases, including 1.49 million asymptomatic patients. The first intensified 100-day campaign under the TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan was launched on 7 December 2024, across 347 high-priority districts in 33 states and Union territories before being expanded nationwide. A second intensified 100-day campaign was launched on 24 March 2026, focusing on screening in 158,000 high-risk villages and wards, congregate settings, and vulnerable populations. cfc2d43380d0d226.headline_en: No MAP relief for taxpayers using safe harbour rules: CBDT
cfc2d43380d0d226.raw_facts: Updated cross-border tax dispute guidelines also clarify how treaty-level resolution interacts with domestic appeals, advance rulings, and settlement schemes under the Income Tax Act, 2025.
flags: Anachronism: The 'Income Tax Act, 2025' does not exist; the current governing law in India is the Income Tax Act, 1961.

Terminology Error: 'MAP relief' (Mutual Agreement Procedure) is a treaty-based mechanism, not typically described as 'relief' in the context of safe harbour rules, which are a separate domestic tax provision.

Logical Inconsistency: Safe harbour rules are a unilateral domestic mechanism to avoid transfer pricing adjustments, whereas MAP is a bilateral treaty mechanism. Stating 'No MAP relief for taxpayers using safe harbour rules' is conceptually confused, as safe harbour users generally do not face transfer pricing disputes that would require MAP.

a6a8b1604feeb9bd.title: How to invest abroad through GIFT City: A step-by-step guide
a6a8b1604feeb9bd.summary: Resident Indians looking to invest abroad can do so through dollar-denominated funds based in GIFT City, the international financial centre in Gujarat. This offers an alternative to investing directly in foreign stocks through overseas brokers, a route examined in an earlier Business Standard article . Here is how to invest through GIFT City, from choosing a fund to transferring money. The route has drawn interest because many international mutual funds from domestic fund houses have stopped taking fresh money. The mutual fund industry as a whole has reached the $7 billion overseas investment limit set by the regulators, and funds based in GIFT City are not subject to that limit. One attraction is regulatory oversight. GIFT City funds come under the International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA), an Indian regulator. Investors using overseas brokers may have limited recourse through Indian regulators if something goes wrong, says Deepesh Raghaw, a Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi)-registered investment advisor and founder of PersonalFinancePlan.in. Those seeking to avoid cross-border disputes may prefer Indian funds or the GIFT City route, he says. Another reason is to hold assets in dollars. The rupee has tended to weaken against the dollar over time, so dollar assets can cushion that fall. Hema Thakkar, head of business development (alternatives) at PPFAS, says investors use these funds to build a dollar corpus for goals like a child’s education abroad, where the bills will be in dollars. A Balasubramanian, managing director and chief executive of Aditya Birla Sun Life Asset Management Company (AMC), also cites overseas education and travel. The market, however, is still developing. GIFT City was established primarily to attract foreign and non-resident Indian (NRI) investment into India, Raghaw says, and outbound retail funds remain a small segment. 6a94123090634351.title: As Chennai Corporation intensifies planting of saplings, waterlogging emerges a deterrent to green cover expansion
6a94123090634351.summary: Published - November 13, 2026 12:52 am IST - CHENNAI Chennai Corporation has started planting two lakh saplings this Northeast monsoon as it seeks to increase green cover in the city from 18% to 33% in a few years. However, waterlogging in several vacant lands, coupled with predominantly clayey soil conditions, remains a challenge to increasing the green cover. Chennai Corporation Commissioner G.S.Sameeran said: “Based on the intensity of rainfall, planting of an estimated 1.5-2 lakh saplings can be achieved by December 2026, in addition to planting 1.36 lakh saplings from June 2026. Our overall target is 12 lakh for this year. It is proposed to prioritise the planting of native tree species such as Mahilam, Poovarasu, Pungam, Punnai, Neer Marudhu, Neem, Jamun and other tropical avenue trees like Peltophorum, Tabebuia, Spathodea and Cassia that are ecologically suitable and well-adapted to the local soil and climatic conditions.” Pointing to site constraints, Dr. Sameeran said waterlogging in several vacant lands, coupled with predominantly clayey soil conditions, posed challenges to tree planting activities and affected the suitability of certain sites for tree planting. As per the Chennai City Biodiversity Index (2025) and the recent assessment by Anna University (2026), Chennai’s existing green cover is estimated to be in the range of 15–18%. Chennai Corporation officials said the civic body proposed to progressively increase Chennai’s green cover towards the 33% benchmark through a comprehensive and integrated approach, comprising large-scale tree plantation across suitable locations, development of urban forests, avenue and roadside plantations, restoration of degraded parks and green spaces. GCC intends to promote partnerships with educational institutions, industries and other organisations. c48eaaec43dc5cd8.title: No government school will be closed due to low enrolment: Minister Rajmohan
c48eaaec43dc5cd8.summary: Published - November 13, 2026 01:13 am IST - VELLORE Minister for School Education, Tamil Development, Information and Publicity, Rajmohan, addresses the Achievers Appreciation Day at VIT Vellore on Thursday. G.Viswanathan, founder & chancellor, VIT, is also seen. | Photo Credit: C. VENKATACHALAPATHY Minister for School Education Rajmohan on Thursday said that the State government will not shut down even a single government school on the basis of low enrollment of students. In his inaugural address at the felicitation ceremony, organised by VIT Vellore, for headmasters of government and government-aided schools in Vellore, Ranipet, Tirupattur and Tiruvannamalai districts that secured 100 per cent pass results in Board examinations for 2023-24, 2024-25 and 2025-26, Mr. Rajmohan said that since the new government formed six months ago, no government school has been closed, citing low enrollment. “New teaching methods such as teaching mathematics through stories and improvements in curriculum have been introduced to boost enrolment in government schools,” he said. G. Viswanathan, founder and chancellor, VIT, highlighted the need to set up a committee to study the impact of the Right to Education Act’s policy of ensuring pass results on overall educational quality and to examine whether the policy need to be reviewed. It comes in the backdrop of closure of around 94,000 government schools as against 51,000 private schools that were opened in the country in the past decade. “In Tamil Nadu, 246 government schools had been shut during the same period. At present, around 1,200 schools have zero enrolment,” he said. Sankar Viswanathan and Sekar Viswanathan, vice presidents, VIT, and Premalatha, District Educational Officer (Vellore), were among others present on the occasion. 4df5d58432614d75.title: Dhinakaran urges quality checks on Children’s Day cakes
4df5d58432614d75.summary: Published - November 13, 2026 01:11 am IST - CHENNAI Amma Makkal Munnetra Kazhagam (AMMK) general secretary T.T.V. Dhinakaran. | Photo Credit: ASHOK R AMMK founder T.T.V. Dhinakaran on Thursday urged the Tamil Nadu government to ensure that cakes procured for distribution to students of government and government-aided schools on Children’s Day were subjected to proper quality checks before being distributed. Mr. Dhinakaran alleged that cakes purchased from various companies had been lying unattended in vehicles for the past four days without proper storage or preservation, raising concerns over their safety. Pointing out that the cakes had reportedly been transported over long distances, Mr. Dhinakaran in a social media post said it was essential to verify their manufacturing and expiry dates, storage conditions and quality. He said reports of improper storage had caused concern among parents, particularly in view of earlier complaints about the quality of food served under the school breakfast and mid-day meal schemes. Mr. Dhinakaran urged the School Education Department to ensure that only safe and quality cakes reached children. aba73b5290c1fc47.title: Five e-scooters catch fire in Ranipet
aba73b5290c1fc47.summary: Published - November 13, 2026 01:02 am IST - RANIPET Police said that an electrical short circuit could have been the reason for the incident. | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT Five electric scooters caught fire at the showroom at Kaveripakkam village near Walajah town in Ranipet on Thursday. Police said that Y. Suresh, 49, a resident of Walajah town, was running an e-scooter showroom on Bazaar Street in Kaveripakkam village near Walajah town. Initial inquiry revealed that, Suresh reportedly plugged in the vehicles to charge the batteries, but apparently forgot to disconnect the power supply before closing the showroom on Wednesday. On Thursday, a few residents alerted Suresh about smoke in the showroom. Police said that when he opened the showroom, Suresh saw that five e-scooters were gutted and 10 other vehicles were damaged in the fire. Based on the alert, firefighters doused the blaze in the outlet. Police said that an electrical short circuit could have been the reason for the incident. They also said that charging the vehicle for too long could have caused the fire, as damaged vehicles were plugged in for charging. A case was registered and further probe is underway. The police said this was not the first time that electric scooters had caught fire. In February 2023, an electric scooter parked on the veranda of a house in Vaniyambadi near Tirupattur caught fire. The vehicle was left to charge the previous night before the owner of the vehicle S. Ihsanuallh, went to sleep. The fire gutted his bike and the meter box. e6f9d26de74449d2.title: SIR: Draft electoral roll released in Vellore, nearby districts
e6f9d26de74449d2.summary: Published - November 13, 2026 01:01 am IST - VELLORE District Collector P.S.Leela Alex releasing the Special draft electoral rolls in the presence of all political parties in Vellore on Thursday. | Photo Credit: C. Venkatachalapathy The draft electoral rolls for Special Intensive Revision (SIR) 2027 were released on Thursday for Vellore, Ranipet, Tirupattur and Tiruvannamalai districts, with women voters higher than men voters. District Election Officer (DEO) P.S. Leela Alex released the draft electoral rolls at the Collectorate in Vellore in the presence of representatives of recognised political parties and district officials. As per the rolls, the draft tally of voters in Vellore district, which comprises five Assembly constituencies, is 11,59,481 voters (5,61,407 men; 5,97,901 women; and 173 others). c416df0d5ce20919.title: Residents urge GCC to stop dumping of waste in Perungudi dumpyard
c416df0d5ce20919.summary: Published - November 13, 2026 12:35 am IST - CHENNAI Citing rising public health issues, residents have demanded that the Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) stop dumping waste in the Perungudi dumpyard. Residents’ associations have planned to launch protests against the dumping. MCN Nagar and State Bank Colony Welfare Association secretary, M. Krishnamurthy, said: “The dumpyard generates leachate when rainwater filters through waste. Leachate seeps into the groundwater and spreads to all the surrounding areas.” K. Kalaiselvam, secretary of the Federation of Thoraipakkam Residents’ Welfare Associations, said the site released toxic air pollutants. Residents have also demanded real-time monitoring of air pollution in the areas near the dumpyard. A. Francis, president of the Federation of Thoraipakkam Residents’ Welfare Associations, said: “Biomining work is progressing at a snail’s pace. It was expected to be completed by 2024, but only 100 acres have been reclaimed so far. Residents are facing the risk of health complications. Chennai Corporation should stop dumping waste and close the dumpyard in Perungudi.” Following protests by north Chennai residents a few years ago, residents of south Chennai are also expected to launch an agitation against the dumpyard. 9a2986172ae2e393.title: Veeramani chargesheet was based on plaint lodged by minor girl
9a2986172ae2e393.summary: Published - November 13, 2026 12:36 am IST - Chennai The chargesheet against Veeramani and two of his drivers, submitted in the designated court for POCSO Act cases, was based on a complaint lodged by a minor girl. According to police sources, the survivor alleged in her complaint that she was sexually exploited by Veeramani. She had identified the octogenarian businessman during an identification process conducted by the special investigation team (SIT). Veeramani is facing seven cases under the POCSO Act and a case of abetment to suicide of a minor in 2004. The cases involve more than 10 survivors who alleged that they were sexually abused by him. The SIT was in the process of finalising the investigation in a few more cases. Prakash Kanniah, one of the accused wanted in connection with the cases, is believed to be in the U.K. After the police took steps to revoke his passport and obtain an arrest warrant from the designated court, which is required to issue a Red Corner notice, he was likely to return sometime this week, a source said. Veeramani and his drivers Parthiban and Babu were charged under various provisions of the Indian Penal Code, POCSO Act and SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act. 0a281acd971cdf13.title: Manappuram Finance Q2 results: Profit jumps over 3-fold to ₹701 crore
0a281acd971cdf13.summary: Gold loan financier Manappuram Finance Ltd on Thursday reported a more than three-fold year-on-year increase in its consolidated profit after tax (PAT) to Rs 701 crore for the September quarter of FY27. The company had posted a PAT of Rs 217.31 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal. On a sequential basis, net profit rose 20 per cent from Rs 585 crore in the June quarter. Total income increased to Rs 3,312 crore in the second quarter of FY27, compared to Rs 2,275 crore in the year-ago period, the company said in a regulatory filing. The company's total assets under management (AUM) stood at Rs 73,303 crore as of September 2026, registering a year-on-year growth of 60 per cent. Gold Loan AUM surged 92.5 per cent YoY to Rs 60,640 crore at the end of the September quarter. Shares of Manappuram Finance settled 0.23 per cent lower at Rs 320.25 apiece on the BSE.

4c1e828f57f7883e.title: Gang held for possession of 500 kg red sanders near Sholinghur in Ranipet
4c1e828f57f7883e.summary: Published - November 13, 2026 01:12 am IST - RANIPET Officials said that the accused told them the consignment was meant to deliver to agents in Chennai. | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT A gang of three persons was arrested after the Forest Department officials seized seven red sander logs weighing around 500 kg from a car near Sholinghur town in Ranipet district on Thursday. The accused were identified them as S. Ramakrishnan, 39, V. Devinthran, 41, and T. Bhagyaraj, 35, all residents of Ranipet. Officials said that they spotted a speeding car during a patrol led by forest range officer N. Saravanan in the Neelakandaranpet Reserve Forest (RF). The team tried to stop the car along with the help of police personnel, but in vain. Forest officials and the police chased the car for around 500 metres and cornered the car at an isolated location near Sholinghur town. The team arrested the three persons after they found red sanders in the vehicle. Officials said that the accused told them the consignment was meant to deliver to agents in Chennai. The gang learnt the forests around Sholinghur town have a sizable number of red sanders that are cultivated by the Forest Department as part of an afforestation programme over a decade ago. A case was registered and the gang members were lodged at Central Prison in Vellore. The seized wooden logs were sent to the government incense sticks making unit in Tirupattur. c3ecb8e0c4add364.title: Saqib takes 7 wickets on debut before rain disrupts Pakistan-Sri Lanka first cricket Test
c3ecb8e0c4add364.summary: Published - November 13, 2026 02:44 am IST - RAWALPINDI Pakistan's Saqib Khan bowls during the fourth day of the first Test cricket match between Pakistan and Sri Lanka, in Rawalpindi, Pakistan, on November 12, 2026. | Photo Credit: AP New fast bowler Saqib Khan's seven-wicket haul led Pakistan's comeback against Sri Lanka on a rain-affected day four of the first cricket test on Thursday. Saqib's dream figures of 7-130 on debut helped Sri Lanka collapse to 446 all out after resuming on a formidable 404-4. Sri Lanka eked out a first-innings lead of 12 runs. Pakistan reached 57-1 in 21.2 overs of its second innings midway into the second session when stumps was called at 3:05 p.m. for bad light followed by rain. Pakistan leads by 45 runs at Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium. At the crease were Azan Awais, on 22 after he was dropped on 17 by captain Kusal Mendis behind the wickets, and Mohammad Taha, one of Pakistan's four debutants who has followed his first innings half-century with 24 not out off 55 balls. The 31-year-old Saqib made full use of perfect bowling conditions on the fourth morning with incisive swing to rattle Sri Lanka. The visitor lost its last six wickets for 42 runs in a seven-wicket first session after only one wicket fell on day two. Saqib became only the fourth man after Mohammad Nazir, Mohammad Zahid and Abrar Ahmed to grab seven wickets in an innings on test debut for Pakistan. “My strength is to bowl out-swingers and I did exactly that today under favorable overcast conditions,” Saqib said. “Yesterday was a bad day for us because we couldn't bowl the way we would have liked to, but coach Mike Hesson told us in the dressing room that if we hit the off stump line and bowl out-swingers we will get wickets.” Saqib kisses the pitchThe greenish pitch on which Sri Lanka lost only Kamindu Mendis on Wednesday sprung to life in on Thursday in overcast conditions. In a relentless eight-over spell, Saqib grabbed 5-25 as centurions Dhananjaya de Silva and captain
